sources.title: https://lni.wa.gov/licensing-permits/electrical/electrical-permits-fees-and-inspections/
sources.supports: Electrical work requires permit and inspection except as in WAC 296-46B-901; permit purchased by contractor or owner doing the work; if hiring a contractor they must buy their own permit; Issaquah is L&I jurisdiction (not a city that does its own electrical); L&I inspects to 2023 NEC; buy permit before starting work

sources.title: https://lni.wa.gov/licensing-permits/electrical/electrical-permits-fees-and-inspections/purchase-permits-request-inspections
sources.supports: Homeowners buy a permit only if doing the work themselves; contact serving utility before disconnect/reconnect/new service; permits good 1 year; request inspection before conceal and within 3 days of completing or 1 day of energizing, whichever first

sources.title: https://www.issaquahwa.gov/146/Permitting
sources.supports: 2018 codes adopted statewide Feb 1, 2021 noted; adopted codes list; MyBuildingPermit.com Check Status; application packets incl Solar Panels (SF and commercial); inspections; Permit Center CPD 130 E Sunset Way, 425-837-3100; virtual appointments

sources.title: https://www.issaquahwa.gov/165/Inspections
sources.supports: Schedule inspections; Today's Inspection List; MyBuildingPermit.com status and corrections; construction hours 7 a.m.-6 p.m. Mon-Fri; Expanded Work Hours Permit for work outside hours; CPD 130 E Sunset Way, 425-837-3100

sources.title: https://www.issaquahwa.gov/183/Do-I-Need-a-Permit
sources.supports: City administers permits only inside city limits; Klahanie and Mirrormont not in City; unincorporated King County goes to King County DPER; Klahanie to City of Sammamish; Permit Center 425-837-3100

sources.title: https://www.issaquahwa.gov/2884/Solar-Panel-Permits
sources.supports: Over 100 solar installations incl. Maple Street Fire Station; SolSmart Gold; most standard residential systems do not need a building permit (L&I electrical still required); consult Solar Checklist; if no, CPD reviews plans; commercial needs building and electrical; shade-free roof and Solar Pathfinder; typical rooftop needs no extra structural engineering except older/unusual buildings; firefighter accessibility via Tip Sheet 24

sources.title: https://www.issaquahwa.gov/3092/Electrical-Permits
sources.supports: Electrical permits reviewed and issued by WA L&I, many online; closest office Bellevue 616 120th Avenue NE Suite C201, 425-990-1400; City of Issaquah business license still required for contractors in city limits

sources.title: https://www.issaquahwa.gov/928/Building-Codes
sources.supports: Adopted codes incl 2021 IBC/IRC/IFC with WA amendments, 2021 Washington State Energy Code; see IMC Title 16.04

sources.title: https://www.issaquahwa.gov/DocumentCenter/View/4605
sources.supports: Building Permit Exemption Checklist for Residential Photovoltaic Systems, 10/06/2025, IRC 2018: 15 yes/no items (dwelling type, licensed contractor, rooftop, engineered PV mounting, lightweight single-layer roof, 18 in height / not above ridge, 3.5 psf, 50 lb point, manufacturer instructions, flashing IRC M2301.2.9, setbacks/height, IRC Ch. 23 and noncombustible or FRT supports, firefighter access Tip Sheet 24, L&I electrical). All yes: no building permit; email checklist to sustainability@issaquahwa.gov; any no: Permit Center 425-837-3100 / CPD@issaquahwa.gov

sources.title: https://www.mybuildingpermit.com/
sources.supports: eCityGov Alliance MyBuildingPermit.com portal used by Issaquah for status, applications and inspections

sources.title: https://www.mybuildingpermit.com/sites/default/files/documentation/Tip%20Sheet%2024%20Residential%20Solar%20Systems.pdf
sources.supports: Tip Sheet 24, July 1, 2016, 2015 IRC/IFC w/ WA amendments: building permit may be required (check jurisdiction); electrical permit always required; firefighter access: strong-point access, 150 ft array, 36 in pathways between arrays and eave-to-ridge except 2:12 or less, 18 in from hip/valley if both sides, 18 in from ridge unless fire chief allows otherwise

sources.title: https://www.pse.com/en/green-options/Renewable-Energy-Programs/customer-connected-solar
sources.supports: Customer Connected Solar: interconnection and net metering; multiple bids; REPs; steps: PowerClerk application, Approval to Construct, install under local codes, electrical final, Notice of Completion, PSE test and meters, approval to energize; Rate Schedule 150; banked credits expire March 31; 100 kW cap; not with TOU 307/327 or schedule 171; availability stated through at least Dec 31, 2025; WA sales-tax exemption mentioned (no dollar figures used)

sources.supports: Material: clamps and brackets for standing-seam metal roofs
